title: OSHA general industry electric power generation, transmission and distribution practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.269, electric power generation, transmission and distribution. Every answer is explained.

questions.question: Under 1910.269(a)(1)(ii)(A), section 1910.269 does not apply to construction work as defined in 1910.12, with which exception?

options.A: Any work done by an electric utility's own employees
options.B: Any work done on lines energized at more than 600 volts
options.C: Line-clearance tree trimming and work involving electric power generation installations as specified in 1926.950(a)(3)
options.D: Any work that lasts longer than 30 days

questions.explanation: Section 1910.269 does not apply "To construction work, as defined in § 1910.12 of this part, except for line-clearance tree trimming and work involving electric power generation installations as specified in § 1926.950(a)(3) of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A factory has supplementary electric generating equipment used to supply the workplace for emergency or standby purposes only. Under the note to 1910.269(a)(1)(i)(A), which part of the rules covers that equipment?

options.A: Subpart S of Part 1910
options.B: Paragraph (v) of 1910.269, on power generation
options.C: Paragraph (u) of 1910.269, on substations
options.D: No OSHA rule covers it

questions.explanation: The note states: "Subpart S of this part covers supplementary electric generating equipment that is used to supply a workplace for emergency, standby, or similar purposes only."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.269(a)(2)(i)(C), what determines the degree of training an employee must receive?

options.A: The employee's years of service with the employer
options.B: The number of employees on the crew
options.C: The size of the employer's service territory
options.D: The risk to the employee for the hazard involved

questions.explanation: The rule states: "The degree of training shall be determined by the risk to the employee for the hazard involved."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An employee will perform a task that is done less often than once per year. How does the note to 1910.269(a)(2)(v)(C) say OSHA considers such tasks?

options.A: As exempt from the training requirements of the section
options.B: As necessitating retraining before the performance of the work practices involved
options.C: As tasks only a contract employer may perform
options.D: As requiring a written test after the work is finished

questions.explanation: The note states that OSHA "considers tasks that are performed less often than once per year to necessitate retraining before the performance of the work practices involved."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: During its work, a contract employer finds an unanticipated hazardous condition that the host employer did not mention. What deadline does 1910.269(a)(3)(ii)(C) set for telling the host employer?

options.A: Within 10 working days after discovering the condition
options.B: Within 2 working days after discovering the hazardous condition
options.C: By the end of the contract
options.D: At the next annual inspection

questions.explanation: The contract employer must advise the host employer of the condition and "shall provide this information to the host employer within 2 working days after discovering the hazardous condition."

questions.question: Employees work on exposed lines energized at 50 volts or more at a remote substation, and there are too few employees for a trained person to reach each exposed employee within the time the rule sets. What does 1910.269(b)(1)(ii) require?

options.A: One trained person must be on call by telephone
options.B: The work must be postponed until a trained person arrives
options.C: A first-aid kit must be placed at each piece of equipment instead
options.D: Each employee at the work location shall be a trained employee

questions.explanation: Where the existing number of employees is too small to meet the requirement "(at a remote substation, for example), each employee at the work location shall be a trained employee."

questions.question: An employee will work alone on a job covered by 1910.269. What does 1910.269(c)(5) require?

options.A: The employer shall ensure that the tasks to be performed are planned as if a briefing were required
options.B: The employee shall hold a job briefing by radio with a supervisor
options.C: The employee may not work alone on any covered job
options.D: The employee shall write a job briefing and file it after the work

questions.explanation: The rule states: "An employee working alone need not conduct a job briefing. However, the employer shall ensure that the tasks to be performed are planned as if a briefing were required."

questions.question: Before any entrance cover to an enclosed space is removed, how does 1910.269(e)(4) require the employer to determine whether it is safe to do so?

options.A: By asking the last crew that worked in the space
options.B: By waiting 24 hours after the space was last entered
options.C: By checking for the presence of any atmospheric pressure or temperature differences and evaluating whether there might be a hazardous atmosphere in the space
options.D: By removing the cover quickly and testing the air afterward

questions.explanation: The employer "shall determine whether it is safe to do so by checking for the presence of any atmospheric pressure or temperature differences and by evaluating whether there might be a hazardous atmosphere in the space."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.269(e)(10), when is the test of an enclosed space's internal atmosphere for flammable gases and vapors performed?

options.A: After the oxygen testing and ventilation required by (e)(9) demonstrate that there is sufficient oxygen to ensure the accuracy of the test for flammability
options.B: Before any oxygen testing, so the flammability result is not disturbed
options.C: Only after the employee has entered the space
options.D: Only if an open flame will be used

questions.explanation: The rule states: "This test shall be performed after the oxygen testing and ventilation required by paragraph (e)(9) of this section demonstrate that there is sufficient oxygen to ensure the accuracy of the test for flammability."

questions.question: Employees work on cable in a manhole. Under 1910.269(t)(8), what must the employer do about the cable's metallic sheath?

options.A: Remove the sheath before work begins
options.B: Paint the sheath to mark the cable being worked
options.C: Nothing, because the rule covers buried cable only
options.D: Maintain metallic-sheath continuity, or treat the cable sheath as energized

questions.explanation: The rule states that "the employer shall maintain metallic-sheath continuity, or the cable sheath shall be treated as energized."

questions.question: Under 1910.269(h)(3), when shall conductive ladders be used in specialized high-voltage work?

options.A: Whenever a nonconductive ladder is not on the truck
options.B: When the employer demonstrates that nonconductive ladders would present a greater hazard to employees than conductive ladders
options.C: Whenever the work is done at night
options.D: Whenever the ladder is shorter than the structure being climbed

questions.explanation: Portable conductive ladders "may not be used near exposed energized lines or equipment. However, in specialized high-voltage work, conductive ladders shall be used when the employer demonstrates that nonconductive ladders would present a greater hazard to employees than conductive ladders."

questions.question: A hydraulic tool's hose may be leaking. What does 1910.269(i)(4)(vi) say employers must ensure?

options.A: That employees find the leak by running a bare hand along the hose
options.B: That employees stop the leak by pressing a gloved hand over it
options.C: That employees do not use any part of their bodies to locate, or attempt to stop, a hydraulic leak
options.D: That employees keep the tool running until the leak is found

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Employers must ensure that employees do not use any part of their bodies to locate, or attempt to stop, a hydraulic leak."

questions.question: A load is suspended from an electric line truck. Under 1910.269(p)(1)(iv), when may the operator leave his or her position at the controls?

options.A: Whenever another employee is watching the load
options.B: Whenever the outriggers are extended
options.C: Whenever the load weighs less than half the truck's rating
options.D: Only if the employer can demonstrate that no employee (including the operator) is endangered

questions.explanation: The operator "may not leave his or her position at the controls while a load is suspended, unless the employer can demonstrate that no employee (including the operator) is endangered."

questions.question: Employees will install new lines parallel to existing energized lines. Under 1910.269(q)(2)(iv), what must happen before they do?

options.A: The employer shall make a determination of the approximate voltage to be induced in the new lines, or work shall proceed on the assumption that the induced voltage is hazardous
options.B: The existing lines shall always be removed first
options.C: The new lines shall be installed only at night
options.D: The employer shall notify OSHA of the work

questions.explanation: The rule states that "the employer shall make a determination of the approximate voltage to be induced in the new lines, or work shall proceed on the assumption that the induced voltage is hazardous."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: During installation of overhead lines, between whom does 1910.269(q)(2)(ix) require reliable communications?

options.A: The pulling-rig operator and the utility's system operator only
options.B: The reel tender and the host employer's safety office
options.C: The reel tender and the pulling-rig operator
options.D: The crew and the local fire department

questions.explanation: The employer "shall ensure that employees maintain reliable communications, through two-way radios or other equivalent means, between the reel tender and the pulling-rig operator."

questions.question: A line-clearance tree trimmer who is not a qualified employee is working near conductors energized at more than 750 volts. Under 1910.269(r)(1)(ii), which condition requires a second line-clearance tree trimmer within normal (unassisted) voice communication?

options.A: The tree is a hardwood species
options.B: Roping is necessary to remove branches or limbs from such conductors or apparatus
options.C: The trimmer is using hand tools only
options.D: The work is done in daylight

questions.explanation: One of the listed conditions is "If roping is necessary to remove branches or limbs from such conductors or apparatus."

questions.question: A climbing rope used by line-clearance tree trimmers has been damaged. What does 1910.269(r)(7)(vi) say about splicing it?

options.A: It may be spliced if the splice is inspected before each use
options.B: It may be spliced by a qualified employee
options.C: It may be spliced if it is then used only near deenergized lines
options.D: Climbing rope may not be spliced to effect repair

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Climbing rope may not be spliced to effect repair."

questions.topic: Substations, generating plants and special conditions
questions.question: An employee who does not regularly work in an attended substation enters it. What does 1910.269(u)(6)(i) require of that employee?

options.A: To sign a visitor log kept at the gate
options.B: To lock the entrance behind him or her
options.C: To report his or her presence to the employee in charge of substation activities to receive information on special system conditions affecting employee safety
options.D: To stay outside the fence until the substation is deenergized

questions.explanation: Each employee other than those regularly working in the station "shall report his or her presence to the employee in charge of substation activities to receive information on special system conditions affecting employee safety."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Substations, generating plants and special conditions
questions.question: Exciter or generator brushes are to be changed while the generator is in service, and the check shows a ground condition exists. What does 1910.269(v)(2) say?

options.A: The brushes may not be changed while the generator is energized
options.B: The brushes may be changed if the employee wears gloves
options.C: The brushes may be changed if the work takes less than 10 minutes
options.D: The brushes may be changed if a second employee watches

questions.explanation: The field must be checked for a ground condition first, and "The brushes may not be changed while the generator is energized if a ground condition exists."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.269, Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Substations, generating plants and special conditions
questions.question: Employees will work on an instrument in a current transformer secondary circuit, and the employer cannot deenergize the primary of the current transformer. What does 1910.269(w)(2) require?

options.A: The secondary shall be opened before work begins
options.B: The employer shall bridge the circuit so that the current transformer secondary does not experience an open-circuit condition
options.C: The work may go ahead with no further step
options.D: The instrument shall be removed while the secondary is open

questions.explanation: Employees may not open the secondary while the transformer is energized, and if the primary cannot be deenergized, "the employer shall bridge the circuit so that the current transformer secondary does not experience an open-circuit condition."
